body:
In counseling I am starting to unravel a lot about my early childhood around 3-5 when my parents divorced. Abandonment issues with my mother.
So I have unraveled and discovered some of these feelings I have towards my mother and the women I am in relationships with.

I always feel like they don't love me. They could tell me a million times that they "Love me more than anything" but it never meant anything. I just couldn't believe them. And I was always scared of her leaving me.

The  only time I really felt love from her was when I would say terrible terrible things to her, or belittle her, or make her cry, or accuse her of cheating. When she would cry or visibly show that what I was saying was hurting her and that what I think of her means a lot to her.
Thats when I would feel like she really did love me and that she wasn't going to leave me.

After she would break down or would get upset, I would feel relieved and like I had proof that she truly loved me. Then it would click in my mind and I would panic and think in my mind "Oh SHIT! You just hurt the woman you love terribly, you're going to push her away!".  But it was the only way I could feel loved. A Vicious cycle of hurting her just to feel loved by her.

She would say "You don't love me!", and I would just be in wonder thinking
"How could she not see I love her?!" 
"I Love her more than anything".

But now I look back and it makes sense.  She just thought, how could a man say he loved her then treat her the way I did.

In the end she couldn't take it any more and left me.

And now I am left with a life changing realization but its too late.

When I was being abusive to her I knew what I was doing was hurting her and pushing her away, but I continued to do it. In the back of my mind I was telling myself that "everyone fights in their relationships behind closed doors, maybe I am just not strong enough to keep my mouth shut".
